newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser says sales up in 1st 16 wks.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser says sales up in 1st 16 wks.

text.p: British department store chain House of Fraser Plc said on Tuesday that like-for-like sales in the first 16 weeks of the current financial years were up 4.9 percent on the same period last year.

While trading in the first 16 weeks has been "encouraging", chairman Brian McGowan told the AGM that "the real prize for your group is margin improvement and it is encouraging that this growth is currently being led by strong increases in sales of womenswear, menswear and perfumeries".
He added that in each of these categories own bought sales had outperformed concessions over the period. Overall, the increase in own bought sales was ahead of concessions.

House of Fraser has been undergoing a major refocusing and last month its executives set a one-year deadline for improvements. The group is trying to refocus on upmarket brand names and quality own-brand merchandise.

McGowan said that while the pace picked up "considerably" over the last year with many operational improvements, "the real effects of our revised strategy will not begin to come through until the second half of the current year, when we will experience the benefits of our improved operating efficiencies".
